standard_prerequisites.name: Separation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For any set V and any property of sets, the collection of elements of V satisfying the property is a set.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof applies Separation to the assumed universal set V and the property x not in x at source lines 880-881.

standard_prerequisites.name: Russell's Paradox
standard_prerequisites.statement: The unrestricted collection of all sets x with x not in x leads to a contradiction.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof closes the reductio by identifying R with that unrestricted collection and invoking the paradox (source lines 881-882).

core_obligations: Assume for reductio that there is a universal set V, so that every set is an element of V (source line 880).

Apply Separation to V with the property x not in x to obtain the set R of exactly the sets that are not elements of themselves, and observe that R coincides with the unrestricted Russell collection because V is universal (source lines 880-881).
Invoke Russell's Paradox for that collection to obtain a contradiction, concluding that no universal set exists (source lines 881-882).

proof_roadmap.step: Assume a universal set V and apply Separation to build R = {x in V : x not in x}.
Identify R with the unrestricted Russell collection and contradict Russell's Paradox.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem thm:NoUniversalSet at source lines 875-877: the set of all sets does not exist. The proof at source lines 879-883 is a short but genuinely two-step argument. It first argues by reductio from an assumed universal set V, and then it must pick the right axiom to apply: it uses Separation with V as the separating set, so that the Russell collection becomes a set, and it identifies that instance with the unrestricted Russell collection of all x with x not in x, which contradicts Russell's Paradox. The step that turns an unrestricted comprehension over the universe into an instance of Separation relative to V is the substance of the argument, and it is exactly the point the statement does not mention. No result outside the retained text is used.
